html:
Israel’s PM Netanyahu has publicly rejected Donald Trump's 15-point peace plan for Gaza, vowing no military withdrawal until Hamas is "genuinely" disarmed. This decision marks a rare public break with the US and has been widely reported as stoking tensions.

US-Iran Tensions & Global Economy: Iran has declared the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US meets its demands, including an end to sanctions, compensation for war damages, and the release of frozen Iranian assets. Oil markets have reacted with price increases amid the uncertainty, particularly following reports of an Iranian missile attack on a UAE tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, condemned by several regional nations. Donald Trump indicates the US is "semi-negotiating" with Iran, noting its "dire economic state" and reportedly preparing to declare victory in the war with Iran even without a nuclear agreement.

Ukraine War & Geopolitical Shifts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claims North Korea may deploy up to 50,000 troops to Russia for the ongoing conflict, with some reports suggesting a North Korean missile unit is already in Russia. This comes as Russia and Ukraine continue to exchange deadly overnight strikes, causing civilian casualties. Meanwhile, Syria and Russia have agreed to end Moscow’s military use of the Hmeimim air base and part of Tartous port, converting them into joint training centers.

Regional Alliances & Military Buildup: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have signed a joint defense agreement, which Turkey's Foreign Minister likened to NATO's Article 5. This pact is seen as having "far-reaching implications for the Middle East," raising concerns about Turkey's military buildup and Saudi Arabia's "growing ties with adversarial nations." Separately, the United States is planning a significant naval buildup, with intentions to construct 19 new nuclear submarines, primarily "with the eyes to China."

Global Security Concerns: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan has been charged in Dublin with directing a criminal organization, following his extradition from Dubai under heavy security. In South Africa, evidence suggesting special forces murdered a top detective has been shared with the BBC. Nigeria's army successfully rescued 33 people kidnapped by gunmen in Zamfara state, and Colombia's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has vowed to crack down on armed drug gangs.

Environmental & Economic Pressures: Catastrophic wildfires continue to rage, with Canada's Bald Range wildfire remaining "out of control" and a wildfire in southern France forcing evacuations. Puerto Rico has begun rationing water supplies due to intense drought and aging infrastructure. In the UK, Andy Burnham has promised a crackdown on "rip-off" business practices to alleviate the cost of living, while Lebanese expats decry soaring prices in Beirut, noting it is reportedly more expensive than Paris.
